correctness.rationale: For all n>=7, the actual GP(n,3) closed-neighbourhood equations over F2 eliminate to the reversible recurrence P3(t)=(1+t)^4(1+t+t²+t³+t⁴). It divides t^20+1, so every solution repeats a 20-word and is gcd(n,20)-periodic. All 256 possible initial eight-bit strings determine a unique periodic solution; exact enumeration gives the six weight tables R1,R2,R4,R5,R10,R20 including 4,10,60,108,60,10,4 at g=20. Independently built GF(2) direct matrix enumerations tested n=7,8,9,10,12,15,20,25,28,30,40,60, and algebraic gcd/degree checks corroborate; finite tests alone are not the infinite proof. All source file blob IDs and the source tree reconstructed exactly.

The earlier general two-colour closed-neighbourhood conflict-free classification applies EXACTLY to the same binary vectors, since every cubic closed neighbourhood has four vertices and a colour is unique iff its red count is 1 or 3.
